System Overview & Research Architecture

About Shape Packing Auto-Researcher

Background, scientific objectives, internal use guidelines, and computational architecture.

Project Purpose

The Shape Packing Auto-Researcher project automates the exploration, verification, and benchmark tracking of 2D polygon packing problems. It is designed to act as an internal workbench for algorithmic development, log analysis, and continuous performance evaluation against Erich Friedman's historical packing benchmarks.

Optimization Engine

Rust & Rayon Numerical Solver

High-throughput multi-start gradient descent, continuous collision penalty minimization, and boundary contraction.

Distributed Grid

Volunteer Compute Coordination

Stateless lease queue protocol connecting standalone native daemons and WebAssembly in-browser workers.

Scientific Verification

Exact Geometric Validation

Automated double-precision polygon containment and non-overlap auditing before record ingestion.

Scientific Reference & Use Notice

This platform serves as an operational dashboard for ongoing algorithm experiments and research tasks. Results displayed on this dashboard reflect automated solver runs and historical reference figures. They are intended for internal system debugging, performance tuning, and geometric visualization, and should not be cited as definitive mathematical proofs without explicit secondary verification.

Reference Citation:
Erich Friedman, "Packing Center", Math Magic, Stetson University.
Historical record comparisons reflect published Friedman benchmark bounds as catalogued in the benchmark dataset.
